advisory.what:
structural.premise_limited is incomplete. A018 can never be killed and is not listed. A018 is mstore_offset +1 at contracts/contracts/libraries/codec/BatchHeaderCodecV0.sol:220, storeSequencerSetVerifyHash: mstore(add(batchPtr, 186), v), and Rollup.sol:351 always passes bytes32(0). It is the same mutant as I22's M018.
- After the mutation, header byte 185 is written by no op. The projection marks it undefined (projection.cells; A-dirty in facts/morph_header.json) on every candidate, so no reading law gets a model hit: no K1 and no masked obstruction.
- replay.m0 runs enc_sol in a fresh frame, where byte 185 is 0. Every PROVED reading law (L_par_hdr_v0/v1, L_rt_go_v0/v1/v2) pins sequencerSetVerifyHash = 0. So the mutant's enc_sol bytes equal the original's at every candidate: no K2 (c) falsification and no partiality.
- The only premise-free reader, L_par_hdr_ssvh, is REFUTED at baseline.
- The survivor lands in proof_lost_unwitnessed, which is an expected class for 'reachable', so structural_agreement will not flag it.
I22's soundness review named exactly this case (M018: 'drops M018-type kills').
Consequence: the ceiling is 96, not 97. threshold.consequence should read e >= 72, not 71 (66 from the panel beyond tce, 37.5% of stratum A).
My byte-level simulation of all 103 reachable mutants (below) finds exactly 7 that cannot be killed: A018 plus the six listed. It confirms the six listed are correct.
advisory.why: The kill rate is unaffected: kills are decided per law at run time by unchanged rules, and the misstatement cannot flip exit (b), since no rule reads the ceiling. But I60's F-A1 and F-A2 are answered by statements, and those statements overstate HOLON's reachable ceiling by one mutant. Fix: state A018 with the six in the review and the report (ceiling 96, e >= 72), and attribute its survival as premise/harness-limited, not as a rule gap.

advisory.what: reporting.plan_literal drops the plan's word 'moves'. The plan's criterion is 'a law moves to REFUTED, with a witness that replays on the mutant code'. The instrument counts 'some predicted law ... REFUTED on the mutant with a Bend-checked counter-law and a hit that replays on the mutant (no two-sided test)', with no condition on the baseline status.
advisory.why: Applied as written, it counts every law that was REFUTED at baseline, is re-decided and still REFUTED, and has a hit that replays on both trees. That covers L_par_hdr_v2 and L_par_hdr_ssvh for every reachable enc_sol or enc_go_v1 mutant, and L_dom_hdr for the ok_go mutants. The premise-limited A018, A162 and A165-A168 would count, and so possibly would the 7 baseline-REFUTED M1x laws. The F-A9 line would then show a near-total 'plan-literal' rate that measures nothing about the mutation. Fix: count only predicted laws whose baseline status is PROVED, UNKNOWN or absent and that move to REFUTED. That is K1 without the two-sided test, which is what F-A9 asked for.

advisory.what:
The kill routes of the reachable class, and what the harness gate covers. In my simulation:
- 78 of the 96 killable reachable mutants can die by K1.
- 17 can die only by K2 (c), a code-level falsification where the model is undefined: A002, A007, A009-A017, A019, A020, A022, A059 (an unwritten A-dirty byte), and A136, A192 (a Go panic, so the cells are undefined). Their only falsifying candidate in the 16-candidate window is 'ones' (A192: 'zeros'; A136: every candidate).
- A081 can die only by a partiality witness.
The planted controls exercise K1 (C1-C3) and partiality (C4), but no control is killed by a K2 (c) code falsification. The gate's 'model' check also compares only where the model is defined.
advisory.why: A defect specific to that route would silently file 17 of the 96 killable mutants (18%; all but A136 and A192 are Solidity header-build mutants) as proof_lost_unwitnessed, and the gate could not see it. This overlaps the soundness lens. Fix: add a K2 (c) control, for example an mstore +1 that leaves an unwritten byte, or report the K2 (c) kills separately (k2_model_tied partly does this).

advisory.what: Survivor class 'masked' cannot be reached by the two structurally masked mutants (A074, A076).
advisory.why: survivor_classes rule 7 asks whether 'every predicted law whose own decided input changed is REFUTED at baseline'. An M0 law's own input hashes the whole projected document (limitations: K2 (a) is per law in name only). My scratch extractions show that A074 and A076 both change load_sol; A074 otherwise changes only enc_sol.walk, which the projection does not read. So ok_sol, and with it the whole projected document, changes, and the 5 PROVED enc_sol laws in their predicted sets count as changed. Both mutants therefore fall through to rule_gap/law_unmoved, while expected_from_structure says 'masked'. structural_agreement will report two disagreements by construction, and two masked survivors get filed as rule gaps. Fix: evaluate rule 7 over structural.M0_reading_laws (or over per-role inputs), or state the effect. Minor: survivor_classes.order lists rule_gap last, but rule_gap/no_law is applied fourth; 'applied' makes the rule order the one that decides.

advisory.what: replay.m0 says the harness has 'memory past the free pointer is zero, as on the deployed path'. On the deployed path this is false when numL1Messages >= 1.
advisory.why: Probe with the pinned forge and solc 0.8.24 (legacy codegen, optimizer off): after an external view call shaped like Rollup._loadL1MessageHashes, the 4 bytes at mload(0x40) hold the low 4 bytes of the call's uint256 argument (0x55667789). That is where the next header allocation starts. The zero-memory harness choice is still preregistered and mechanical. It matters only for mutants that leave header bytes 0..3 unwritten (A002 leaves byte 1): their K2 (c) falsification shows a zero where the deployed byte is dirty, so it holds at function level only. Fix: drop the 'as on the deployed path' justification, or state this.

advisory.what: Nothing freezes holon/mutate once the first catalog record is committed.
advisory.why: The gate must pass 'at the records' pipeline_commit' and must be 'first committed before any catalog mutant's record'. Fixes are described only for failed gate attempts, when 'no catalog mutant has run by then'. The instrument does not say that all catalog records share one pipeline commit. It also does not say that a change to holon/mutate (projection or harness) made after a catalog record exists is an amendment that reruns every mutant and keeps the earlier records. Without that, a change made after seeing outcomes could pass through a new gate attempt unremarked. State it.

advisory.what: own_input and the baseline precondition leave path and provenance details to the builder.
advisory.why: law_sets.own_input keys 'facts' by path, but the path of a mutant's projected document is not fixed; only the committed gen/M2/mutation_i61/header.projected.json is named. If each mutant uses its own scratch path, three things follow for every mutant with predicted M0 laws: K2 (a) becomes trivially true, carrying never applies to M0, and survivor rule 6 (extraction_gap/model) becomes unreachable. Fix: pin the logical path for every run. preconditions.baseline compares the extracted documents normalized but does not say so for the projection. A scratch extraction records target.commit null (I verified this: on a copy of the null tree both Solidity sidecars normalize to the committed documents). If the projection copies that target, a byte comparison with the committed projection fails. Say 'normalized' there too. Two of the projection's inputs are also implied rather than named: the Go struct-field to Header-field map (I16's binding) and how ok_sol is derived from load_sol.

advisory.what: The rules do not fix which K2 (c) candidate is recorded.
advisory.why: (c) only asks whether some candidate among the first 16 qualifies, of two kinds (falsification or partiality). Three things depend on which one is recorded: model_tied (reporting.k2_model_tied), falsifier.role/revert_line, and the gate's 'K2 with the named falsifier kind'. Fix: record the first qualifying candidate in refuter order, and prefer falsification over partiality at the same candidate.

advisory.what: not_K2's 'a generator returning None' should name the baseline's accepted generator.
advisory.why: version_split returns None for every Header law, and holon/pipeline.prove skips it without recording an attempt. Under the broad reading, every lost Header-law proof would become an error and K2 could never hold. The context of (b) implies the narrow reading, and C4 would expose the broad one at the gate, but the wording should say it.

advisory.what: The rules do not classify a law decided REFUTED whose replay cannot run.
advisory.why: kill_criterion.errors marks 'the law whose witness it replays' as error, but 'never a law the run decided otherwise', and 'decided' counts a Bend-checked REFUTED as decided. Read literally, no hit of such a law replays, so it is a replay disagreement and sets extraction_defect_detected. Fix: say that a replay harness failure makes the law's K1 determination an error, never a replay disagreement. This is unlikely in practice: every catalog mutant compiles and builds.

advisory.what: The gate has three gaps: its order relative to the baseline, ok_sol on a mutated tree, and revert-line checking.
advisory.why: Control kills are judged against the baseline record, because K1 and K2 compare statuses and own inputs. Yet preconditions.order says the gate needs nothing before it. State that a reproducing baseline record exists before `holon mutate gate` runs. No control runs ok_sol on a mutated tree; the masked obstructions and equivalence contradictions of A074 and A076 depend on it, though no kill does. C4 accepts any line in enc_sol's revert_lines, so a harness that reports the wrong revert line still passes. That is harmless for kills, because only :293 is copied.

advisory.what: 'reachable (entry-fit)' treats computed header fields as free.
advisory.why: On the deployed path, batchIndex is the parent's index + 1 and totalL1MessagePopped is the parent's total plus numL1Messages. dataHash, blobVersionedHash and parentBatchHash are hashes the caller does not choose. Entry-fit checks only the unprojected requires and the value types. The instrument calls this an approximation, which is honest. Listing these fields would make the gap explicit.

The controls' offsets, original text and mutant_sha256 reproduce. It copies only the require at :293, because the conditions of :294 and :295 past the earlier paths are on prevStateHash and postStateHash. The version expression is batchDataInput.version (the value argument of storeVersion at :342), read as the witness's version at :293, :333 and :353. The innermost block is :330-374; its statements :332 to :354 are copied. Store values are bound from the witness: version as uint8; batchIndex, l1MessagePopped, totalL1MessagePopped and lastBlockNumber as uint64; the six hashes as bytes32. The zeros store at :351 keeps the tree's text. The local _batchPtr is declared uint256. The sink at :357 becomes a return of _headerLength bytes from _batchPtr, using I16's copy. Run with the pinned forge and solc on 256 candidates (4 enc_sol laws x 64): the null tree executes on all 256 and equals the hand model's enc_sol on all 256 (I60's harness executed 0 of 64). Mutated trees: A081 reverts at the copied require ('invalid version') on every v2 candidate, and C4 on every v1 and v2 candidate. C3 and A058 return 249 bytes at v1 (C3 also at v2). A059 leaves bytes 249..256 zero at v1. C1, A022 and A027 change bytes 25-26, 249 and 1. So mutated lines of the entry function (:293, :333, :353) and library mutants all execute. Extractors on scratch trees: scratch Solidity extraction (sidecars with target.commit null) of the null tree normalizes equal to both committed documents. Scratch Go extraction of the 5 documents is byte-identical. Solidity extraction succeeds for C3, C4, A081, A058, A059, A074 and A076 with the expected path changes (C4 version bound 0, A081 '<' 2, C3 and A058 length 249 at v1, A059 11 ops at v1). Go extraction of C2 puts BatchIndex at bytes 3..10. M0 pipeline (holon run --no-registry, Bend 2.0.36) on hand facts edited the way the projection would edit them for those extractions: for C4, L_par_hdr_v1, L_rt_go_v1 and L_rt_go_v2 end UNKNOWN, with open_refl exit 1, first line 'SOME PROOFS FAIL', 64 of 64 candidates undefined, and the generated model checked alone giving 'ALL PROOFS CHECK'. For A081, L_rt_go_v2 ends UNKNOWN; for A059, L_par_hdr_v1 and L_rt_go_v1 end UNKNOWN. C3 makes L_par_hdr_v1 REFUTED and C1 makes L_par_hdr_v0 REFUTED. All four controls can therefore be killed as preregistered. Bend probe: a rejected proof, a parse error and a type error all print 'SOME PROOFS FAIL' and exit 1. A model checked alone prints 'ALL PROOFS CHECK' only when it parses and type-checks. So K2 (b)'s model check separates a proof rejection from an error in a generated file. Conclusion: I60's S-B1 is fixed (all five parts are implemented and the harness now overlaps every refuter candidate), and S-A1 to S-A10 are each answered in the rules. K1 and K2 are stricter than the plan's verbatim criterion, never looser.
